messages:
oncall-bot: PAGER — gpu_pool_saturation (eu-west-1 / gpu-pool-3): pool_util >= 95% for 12m. Pager: emily

emily: seeing huge queue growth in the last 8m, latency spiking. autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts but new nodes stuck in provisioning.

ashwin: confirming — API metrics: request_queue length 2384, 99th latency 11.2s, token throughput down 45% for requests routing to this pool.

emily: job: triage. i'll take lead. @sre-latasha can you check node provisioning + cloud provider errors?

sre-latasha: on it. initial look -> provider API returning 429s for instance create. provisioning backoff hitting our autoscaler circuit. logs: `ProvisionRequestFailed: rate_limit_exceeded` repeated.

sam: tagged as SEV-2 for customer-impact. which customers affected? support-ana: rough list from routing -> ~12 customers clipped, 3 on dedicated, rest on hosted but pinned to eu-west region.

support-ana: we have customer-reported API 503s starting ~12:02 UTC. sending heads-up to CS.

ashwin: quick mitigation options: 1) divert non-critical tenants to a different region/model, 2) temporarily throttle ephemeral low-priority queues, 3) force scale by adding instances via control plane (manual).

emily: can we cold-start instances in other azs? last time region-wide rate limits prevented cross-az as well.

sre-latasha: provider rate limits are account-wide for this region. cross-az spawns also hit 429. but we can spin up smaller instance types that are not rate-limited? need approval.

ops-lead-raj: recommend immediate 1) enable tenant throttling policy, 2) toggle fallback routing to eu-central for non-enterprise traffic, 3) open bridge if not already.

emily: starting throttling rule now. patching routing table to reduce requests to gpu-pool-3 by 60%. applying canary to 10% first.

ashwin: command to apply throttling (internal):
```bash
curl -X POST https://console.api/redwood/ops/throttle -d '{"pool":"gpu-pool-3","reduce_pct":60,"tenants":"non-enterprise"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN"
```

emily: ran it at 12:11 UTC — canary shows initial queue decrease. queue down from 2384 -> 1600.

sam: good. still need capacity. will try manual spawn of smaller instances. @sre-latasha can you attempt manual create of 4 x gpu-small?

sre-latasha: attempting manual create via provider console now — hitting 429s but partial success: 2 of 4 spawned, reporting `InstanceReady` at 12:18 UTC.

emily: routing started to those nodes. acceptance tests show lower tail latency for some tenants.

jordan: autoscaler analysis — looks like autoscaler entered hot-loop backoff after repeated ProvisionRequestFailed. scale policy has exponential backoff up to 20m. we hit HWM while backoff active.

ashwin: that means even with manual intervention, autoscaler won't try more until backoff ends. need to override backoff in control plane.

ops-lead-raj: @jordan can you lift autoscaler backoff? set backoff to minimal and force one scale op.

jordan: done at 12:22 UTC — forced scale op succeeded creating 3 more small instances. queue down to 720.

emily: rolling routing back to normal for enterprise customers only; small degrade persists for low-priority tenants. customer-facing incidents page updated: "Partial service degradation for EU region, mitigation in progress".

support-ana: posted to customers, added affected customer list. engineering escalated.

oncall-bot: BRIDGE OPEN — #incident-1823456789-bridge

emily: starting bridge for live coordination. bridge link: https://meet.redwood/incident-1823456789

sre-latasha: manual mitigation summary: - throttled non-critical tenants - spun up 5 small instances (2 manual, 3 forced) - forced autoscaler out of backoff. Observed provider 429s continue but at lower rate.

ashwin: routing metrics look stable now. queue at 410 and dropping. 99th latency 2.3s.

sam: customer impact: 12 customers saw degraded response times, 3 reported 5xx. none had data loss. support team proactively issued credits to 3 customers.

emily: can we mark this as mitigated? still watching for 30m.

ops-lead-raj: agree to monitor. immediate postmortem actions to start: identify why autoscaler backoff didn't consider provider 429 as transient vs terminal; add override path for manual scale when backoff active; implement regional fallback routing for low-priority traffic automated.

jordan: logs + trace snippet showing autoscaler state machine: 
```json
{"time":"12:05","event":"ProvisionRequestFailed","code":429,"attempt":3,"backoff_ms":1200000}
```

(emily): noted. need blameless root cause: provider rate-limiting + autoscaler aggressive backoff + lack of automated cross-region fallback.

support-ana: CS update posted at 12:40 UTC: short degradation, mitigations applied, ETA for full recovery 30m.

sre-latasha: by 12:50 UTC queue stable <100, latency back to normal. bridging out in 15m if stable.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring

emily: closing bridge at 13:10 UTC. creating follow-up doc in #postmortems. assigning action owners.

jordan: creating a quick runbook PR for "Autoscaler: provider-rate-limit backoff override" and add test harness. assigning to me + emily.

ops-lead-raj: action items (brief):
- raj: runbook + emergency override implementation (ETA 1w)
- emily: cross-region fallback automation proposal (ETA 2w)
- jordan: autoscaler logic change to interpret provider 429 as transient with capped retry fastpath (ETA 1w)
- sre-latasha: add metrics to detect autoscaler backoff causing queue growth (ETA 3d)
- support-ana: customer communication template + credits audit (ETA 2d)

support-ana: I will follow up with the customers who reported 503s and confirm credits.

emily: tagging for postmortem: sev2, duration ~1h10m, peak queue 2384, customers impacted ~12, no data loss.

jordan: PR link for quick patch (wip): https://git.redwood/infrapulse/PR-3421

sre-latasha: saved logs + provider request traces to incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/1823456789/

emily: good work team. closing thread once postmortem doc created. please add any additional notes here. :thumbsup:

support-ana: added note: CS received 2 angry emails, we replied w/ interim explanation and credits.

ashwin: note for follow-up: evaluate ability to spawn non-GPU fallback for low-priority requests with degraded quality but available capacity.

emily: ended thread — will paste postmortem link when created.
